### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/hook-body.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via lowerCallables (symbol, a top-level function), api.read (literal, a string literal in reboundCapabilities), crypto.uuid (literal, a string literal in reboundCapabilities))_
- `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`  _(via api.read (literal, a string literal in reboundCapabilities))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via api.read (literal, a string literal in reboundCapabilities))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via extractHookBody (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/hook-body.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5ce5a51ba0fc673cf22f534e022ccc3f0342c08b` — the merge of head `2970d13e0714ea871960257d0d5ef2ce97ea5c63` into base `6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5ce5a51ba0fc673cf22f534e022ccc3f0342c08b && git checkout 5ce5a51ba0fc673cf22f534e022ccc3f0342c08b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f 2970d13e0714ea871960257d0d5ef2ce97ea5c63 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f && git merge --no-ff 2970d13e0714ea871960257d0d5ef2ce97ea5c63

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6364375b51f6a301681185a78839115a9ccbd19f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a27cba27810eb9775731c52c8048fe94b10ba0ba`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22837 (body and all four comments: the triage direction 6109239514, the claim 6109397230, the dev report 6110163358, the seat answer 6110191438), PR #22859 (body, 14-file list, net diff), the check-runs on the head, and for context only the base sources on `origin/main` (`extract-hook-body.ts`, `detect-free-identifiers.ts`, `lower-callables.ts`, `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts`, `body-runner.ts`, `quickjs-runner.ts`, `hook.zod.ts`, objectql `engine.ts` and `hook-wrappers.ts`, `hook-bodies.mdx`, `examples/app-todo`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `turbo.json`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`), plus the `lower-callables.ts` patch of PR #22849 for the overlap. Nothing was built, run or ablated.

**Check-runs on the head, latest per name (33 runs).** Completed success: Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger, Type Check source gates, filter. Completed skipped: Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in). **Still `in_progress` at read time, with no conclusion: Lint & Repo Gates, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core (1/6) through (6/6), Type Check workspace.** Those nine are not green; they are unanswered. The derived test families (the two new cli pins, the eight targeted cli files, the dogfood door) and the repo gates the dev ran locally (`check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:changeset-no-major`, lint) have as yet no CI conclusion on this head. The Dogfood Regression Gate shards, which are complete and green, are the only CI reading of the door.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The rebind on the hook face: right.** `planHookParameterRebind` reads the parameter off the same `parseFunction` node the free-identifier pass uses, so the two cannot disagree on what the parameter binds; the prologue `var PARAM = ctx;` (or `var PATTERN = ctx;`, the pattern's text verbatim, pattern-internal defaults included) is emitted as the body's first statement. Checked against the two contracts it relies on: the runtime's L2 wrapper binds exactly `ctx` for hooks (`quickjs-runner.ts:328`) and `(input, ctx)` for actions (`:333`); objectql calls an in-process hook handler with exactly one argument (`hook-wrappers.ts:370` and `:376`, `engine.ts:4651` and `:5110`). So the handler's one parameter IS the context, and `var` is the right spelling: a parameter is a mutable, function-scoped binding, a `const` would TypeError on a handler that reassigns it (pinned, "lets the body reassign its parameter") and a `let` or `const` would SyntaxError against a body `var` of the same name. The ruling's literal `const` was illustrative; `var` is what "the author's code then runs as written" requires. A `ctx`-named or parameterless handler takes `NO_REBIND`, `source` is then `block.source` unchanged and `reboundCapabilities` adds nothing: byte-identical, and pinned by equality with the action face over six shapes. The action face is untouched: no prologue, the three new patterns carry `face: 'hook'` and are skipped, and the capability and forbidden scans run over `block.source` exactly as on the base. `lowerCallables` and the `os lint` rule pass the face of the slot, so the #3782 parity holds by construction.

2. **The residue refused as `forbidden-token`, naming the parameter: each right.** Several parameters (the second has nothing to bind to; a `(ctx, extra)` handler is refused even with `extra` unused, which is correct because the in-process call passes one argument). A default (not reproducible as a plain binding). A rest parameter. A pattern binding the name `ctx` (the prologue would read its own left-hand side). A body declaring `ctx` or the parameter's own name with `let`/`const`/`class`/`function` at the body's top level, or `function` in a nested block: each a real divergence, not an over-refusal. The TDZ case (`const ctx = hookCtx.input` after `var hookCtx = ctx;`) is a ReferenceError; a top-level `function hookCtx(){}` is initialised at entry in-process but overwritten by the prologue's assignment once lowered; the nested-block `function hookCtx(){}` is the Annex B case the docblock names, where in-process the parameter name blocks the var-hoist and lowered the prologue's `var` is exactly the binding the block function clobbers. `var` of the parameter's name is correctly not refused (same binding). A capability-bearing member (`api`, `log`, `crypto`, `title`) destructured further than one plain name is refused because `reboundCapabilities` could not follow it and the sandbox would refuse the body at run time; the plain-name control lowers. One further narrowing the changeset does not name: on the hook face a handler whose source `parseFunction` cannot resolve to one node is now refused `unparseable`, where the base tolerated `unparsed` and lowered the body with no free-identifier check. I found no handler shape `peelToBlockBody` accepts that the three wraps plus the span check reject (arrow, anonymous and named function expression, method shorthand, `new Function` output all resolve), so this is the safe direction on a theoretical set. Right.

3. **The three new member refusals and the one exception: each a real absence, and the exception's reason is true.** Read independently from the two sources. `HookContextSchema` (`hook.zod.ts:494` on) declares `id`, `object`, `event`, `input`, `result`, `previous`, `submitted`, `dispatch` (`mode`, `index`, `scope`), `session`, `provenance`, `referentialFieldClear`, `transaction`, `ql`, `api`, `user`. `buildSandboxContext` (`body-runner.ts:1061` on) returns `input`, `previous`, `user`, `session`, `event`, `object`, `result`, `api`, `log`, `title`, `dispatch` as `{ mode, index }`, `inputOptions`, a conditional `referentialFieldClear`, `crypto`. Absent from the body: `dispatch.scope`, `id`, `provenance`, `ql`, `submitted`, `transaction`, exactly the pin's six. All five hook-context literals in objectql's `engine.ts` (`:12923`, `:13217`, `:14276`, `:15589`, `:18205`) set `provenance`, `transaction` and `ql`; none sets `id`, so `id` is `undefined` on both faces and the exception's reason holds, as does its second half (refusing `id` would refuse every `row.id` read off a root-bound record). The exemption of `ctx.api.transaction(fn)` is a published body route already (`hook-bodies.mdx:136` on `main`; the body's `api` passes the engine's scoped api through), and `hookContextMemberRx` cannot reach it anyway: `api` after a dot is not a root receiver, and the call-exempt lookahead covers `api.transaction(` off a root alias. A field named `provenance`, `ql` or `transaction` under `ctx.input` or `ctx.previous` is not refused (pinned). `row.ql` off a root-bound record is over-refused, the safe direction the file already accepts for `submitted`.

4. **Parameter-list destructuring meeting the member refusals: right for what it claims, with a bounded residual.** `var { input, submitted } = ctx;` meets `SUBMITTED_RX`'s destructured limb, and `var { dispatch: { scope } } = ctx;` meets `DISPATCH_SCOPE_RX`'s fourth limb (`dispatch\s*:\s*\{[^{}]*\bscope`), both pinned. The residual: every destructured limb is written `\{[^{}]*\bMEMBER\b[^{}]*\}`, so a member destructured beside a nested pattern (`async ({ submitted, previous: { status }, input })`) or itself destructured one level (`async ({ provenance: { flowRunId } })`, the natural spelling for an object member) escapes it, lowers, and reads `undefined` or TypeErrors at run time: the family's failure. The body spelling has the same limit on `main`, so the changeset's sentence "now meets the refusal the body spelling meets" is literally true, and the PR's docblock scopes the three members to "the spellings `SUBMITTED_RX` reads". Not blocking. The handler's parameter node is already in hand (`bindingNames`, the binding elements' property names), so an exact check of the pattern's top-level keys against the absent set would close the parameter-list half for nothing; recommended on the corrected head or on the family's route (#22860's card), the seat's call.

5. **The enumeration pin: derived, able to fail, and declared.** `inProcessFace` walks the `HookContextSchema` initialiser to the root `z.object` literal through `lazySchema` and the builder chain, one level into a member whose root is itself `z.object`, dropping `retiredKey` tombstones; `bodyFace` finds `function buildSandboxContext`, takes its last `return` literal, resolves a shorthand through the function's locals (so `dispatch` yields `{ mode, index }` out of the conditional), reads `engineCtx?.MEMBER` as passthrough, and a spread as a conditional member. I walked both readers against the sources by hand and they produce the six paths the "classifies today" snapshot lists. The anti-vacuity test requires known members on both faces and a non-empty absent set, so an empty derivation cannot pass; the stale-exception test reds an exception the derivation does not need; the dev's ablations a and b are the two failure modes that matter and both are reported red on exactly one path. The snapshot test is a hand list, but it sits beside the derived checks as a visible-diff pin, not in place of them. The two reads are declared where AGENTS.md requires: `@objectstack/cli` `globs` in `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `@objectstack/cli#test` inputs in `turbo.json`, single files, not trees. The stated blind spots (`api`'s own members, depth beyond one level, the action face) are honest and the first is pinned elsewhere.

6. **The `parseFunction` span check: a real defect on the base, correctly repaired, and an accept-set change in both directions.** A method shorthand in the first wrap parses as a call followed by a block; with exactly one function nested in that block, that nested function was the only function-like node and was returned as the handler. The span comparison (`getStart` equals the prefix length, `end` equals prefix plus source) rejects it and the object-literal wrap reaches the method; the CONTROL test shows arrow and function expression were never affected. The rebind depends on it (without it the nested arrow's parameter would be rebound). Its effect on the public doors: a method local closed over by the nested function is no longer reported free, so that handler lowers where `--strict-body` exited 1 and `os lint` warned (a widening); a module-scope helper called outside the nested function is now reported, so that handler is refused where it lowered and threw (a narrowing). Judged in ②.

7. **The door and the corpus: right.** `lbd_param` moves from documenting the `500` to proving the rebind (never deleted), `lbd_destructure` is added beside it, `lbd_two` rides with `lbd_stash` as a refused handler kept out of the booted artifact. The corpus claim is verified on `main`: `examples/app-todo/src/objects/task.hook.ts:54` names its parameter `ctx`, reads `ctx.input.data` at `:55` (absent on the body face, so the lowered body returned at `if (!data) return;`) and `ctx.ql` at `:100`; it now bundles, where it runs in-process again. No example file changes; the other three examples have no non-`ctx` handler parameter and no root read of the three members (`git grep` on `main`). That move is stated in the PR body and the dev report, not in the changeset or the docs; acceptable, since the example is not a published surface and nothing in it moves, though a line in the changeset would have cost nothing.

8. **Public surface: unchanged, as claimed.** `extractHookBody`'s signature and refusal kinds are the same; `extractLoweredBody` and `LoweringFace` are exported from the utils module only, not from the published `@objectstack/cli/hook-body` subpath (`hook-body.ts` changes its docblock only). No `packages/runtime` or `packages/spec` edit. Every one of the 14 files is inside the claim as widened by edit before the ACCEPT. The overlap with PR #22849 on `lower-callables.ts` is the same four lines adding `ref` there and `face` here; the two do not conflict in meaning, and the resolution `tryExtractBody(fn, originLabel, ref, face)` is mechanical.

9. **The `hook-bodies.mdx` edit: every sentence true against the diff.** The new bullet (the three members, `undefined` for `provenance`, live host objects for `ql` and `transaction`, `ctx.api.object(name)` and `ctx.api.transaction(fn)` not affected, the derivation sentence); "these refuse the body, not the handler" with the three doors; the new paragraph on the parameter (the two emitted spellings, byte-identical for `ctx` or none, the residue list, the action's `(input, ctx)` left alone). All hold.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `@objectstack/cli: minor`, declared BREAKING with the bang: the right level.** The residue's refusals and the three member refusals narrow what `objectstack build` lowers at three public doors (the build's warning and bundled fallback, `--strict-body` exit 1, `os lint` `hook-body/bundled-fallback`); the family's convention is minor-with-BREAKING and `check:changeset-no-major` (inside Check Changeset, green) accepts it. Each BREAKING bullet is true against the diff, including the sixth (an `(input, ctx)` target passed to the published `extractHookBody` is refused for its second parameter while `objectstack build` lowers it on the action face). The fifth bullet records "It now lowers" for the method-shorthand shape: the changeset itself states a widening.
- **The ADR-0087 marker** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the reasoning holds (a build-time verdict about handler code; no authorable key, export, spelling or stored shape moves; a refused handler keeps running bundled). The registration gate's signal is read from the arm (`clause-②-narrowing`), which the correction below does not change. Its CI conclusion sits under Lint & Repo Gates, in progress at read time.
- **The `Clause-②` line: the citation does not cover the shape, and the line must be `yes (narrowing)`.** The seat kept `no (narrowing)` on `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx:169` as published text that already denied the refusal. Judged against the shape (a method shorthand with exactly one nested function, closing over a method local, refused as `free-identifiers` on the base): (a) line 169 is one bullet, "references to identifiers from value-only top-level imports", in the list "The CLI builder rejects any source that uses". It names one rejection cause; it says nothing about method shorthands, nested functions or a handler's own locals, so it neither promises nor denies anything about this shape. (b) Reading that list as exhaustive, which is what the seat's inference needs, is not available: the same document at `:276` names "a module-scope identifier" as a refusal cause beyond line 169's imports, and the base refuses a module-scope `const` helper that is no import. Silence at 169 is therefore not a promise of acceptance. (c) The change is measured at two public doors: `--strict-body` moves from exit 1 to exit 0 and `os lint` from a warning to silence for a shape that was refused, while the same fix also narrows (a module-scope helper outside the nested function is now refused). That is the definition of the `yes (narrowing)` arm in `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read." The dev's recommendation (option A) is right. The correction is to the PR body and `.changeset/22837-lowered-hook-parameter-rebind.md` line 13, both to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The level stays `minor` (both arms take at least minor) and the ADR-0087 disposition is unchanged (the arm is still `narrowing`).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
1. `var` not the ruling's `const`: accepted, see ① item 1; it is the only spelling with a parameter's semantics.
2. Three member refusals the card did not name: they are the triage ruling's own refuse-or-exception rule applied to what the pin derived; each verified absent (① item 3). Accepted.
3. `parseFunction` span check under the bounded exemption: the defect is real, the rebind depends on it, the fix is one span comparison, no other open claim holds the file (#22849 edits `lower-callables.ts` only; #22841 is held). Accepted as a fix; its Clause-② consequence is ruled in ②.
4. Files beyond the claim's first surface: all named in the claim as widened before the ACCEPT; no runtime or spec edit. Accepted.
5. Clause-②: answered in ②, `yes (narrowing)`; the seat corrects the claim, the PR body and the changeset, as it undertook in 6110191438.
6. Overlap with #22849: read both patches; no meaning conflict; whichever lands second merges `main`. Not a finding.
7. `origin/main` merged into the branch before the final gate run: fine.
8. `pnpm lint` as a proven narrowing rather than a run: the three pieces of evidence are coherent, but the repo-wide verdict is CI's, and Lint & Repo Gates has no conclusion yet on this head. Pending, not green.

The one `open_questions` entry (keep `no (narrowing)` or correct to `yes (narrowing)`): **A, correct it**, see ②.

Out-of-scope findings:
- The regex body-peel counting braces through strings and the inner-arrow mis-peel: filed as #22860, not this PR's scope. Noted that the rebind's prologue is read off the TypeScript node while the body it is prepended to is still the regex peel's, so a mis-peeled body is mis-peeled with its prologue; that is #22860's repair, and the right body span is already on the node this PR reads.
- The action face's parameter question (`(params, context)` loses both names): a real member of the same family on the other face, outside this card's lane; the lint pin that keeps `(input, ctx)` silent is correct for the action wrapper. Escalated to the seat as a card to file, not a finding here.
- `os lint`'s write-set extractor not following a rebound receiver: a pre-existing coverage gap (an in-body `const c = ctx` has the same hole), not a regression. For the seat.
- `app-todo`'s `task_logic` bundling: verified (① item 7).

My own, for the seat: the nested-pattern residual in ① item 4 (non-blocking, a small exact check on the parameter node would close it); and the nine check-runs without a conclusion at read time, which this record does not call green.
